No ṭāghūt verse contains any ṭaghā verb and no verse glosses ṭāghūt from the root, so its 'false-deity-because-of-excess' derivation is asserted, never Quran-internally demonstrated.
Tgy.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each independently reached the same nucleus and the same single resistant class (ṭāghūt), with no lens able to bridge it Quran-internally.

mrA.candidate_root_contribution: For the nominal family (37/38 tokens) the root م ر أ contributes 'a single, countable, individuated adult human person' — inherently singular/dual (never a native plural; the collective is suppleted by naas/nisaa'/rijaal), gender-marked by morphology (masc. imru'/al-mar'/imra' 'a/the man, the individual'; fem. imra'a 'a woman'), and inherently neutral in quality. The feminine specializes to 'wife' only under annexation/possessive to a male (construct or pronoun), never lexically; the masculine never reciprocally specializes to 'husband'. There is NO verbal/eventive realization of this root in the corpus. The 38th token, the adjective marī' (4:4), denotes 'wholesome/agreeable to consume' and is a separate, Quran-internally unbridged lexicalized class, not covered by this contribution.
mrA.plain_explanation: Across 37 of 38 occurrences the root names a human being as one discrete individual — a man (imru', al-mar', or the bare masculine imra' in 19:28 'a man of evil') or a woman (imra'a). It is never a collective 'mankind/men/women'; plurality shows only as duals (imra'atayn 28:23, imra'ataan 2:282) or as distributive 'every individual' (kullu imri'in). 'Wife' is not a meaning of the word: imra'a means 'wife' only when bound to a male (imra'atu fir'awn, imra'atuhu), and stays plain 'woman' when unbound (the ruling woman 27:23, the two women 28:23, the witnessing pair 2:282, the believing woman 33:50, the woman fearing her husband 4:128 who is married yet whose marriage is carried by ba'l, not by imra'a). The single remaining token, marī' at 4:4 ('eat it wholesome and agreeable'), describes palatable food and has no Quran-internal path to 'human individual'; it is a homonymous lexicalized isolate that keeps the whole-root claim from being STRONG or universal.
mrA.strongest_counterexample: 4:4:14:1 «فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيٓـًٔا مَّرِيٓـًٔا»: the sole ADJ token, marī', denotes food/gift being wholesome and agreeable to consume, with zero human-individual content; Quran-internally there is no bridge from 'wholesome-to-consume' to 'a human person', so 4:4 is a lexicalized homonymous isolate that resists the human-individual nucleus and caps the whole-root claim.
mrA.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) each partitioned the 38 tokens identically into person-family (37) plus marī' (1) and each proposed MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE for the whole root, converging without coordination.

Awy.candidate_root_contribution: An animate entity coming-to-settle / being-lodged at a locus reached as destination-abode. Form I (intransitive + إلى): the subject betakes itself to / takes up lodging at a fixed point. Form IV (causative-transitive): an agent lodges/houses/takes in another. Noun مَأْوَىٰ (maf'al place-noun): the place where that settling terminates — the abode one ends up in. The nucleus is valence-neutral: safety, benefit, permanence and polarity are context-supplied, not root-entailed.
Awy.plain_explanation: The root paradigm is a clean three-cell valence set: أَوَى (I) = settle oneself at a place (Cave, rock, mountain, a strong support), always intransitive with إِلَىٰ + terminus; آوَى (IV) = the morphological causative, lodge/harbour/take another in (Joseph draws his brother to himself, God shelters the orphan, the Anṣār give shelter); and مَأْوَىٰ = the resulting place-of-settling. The intuitive reading 'refuge/shelter/safe haven' fits every verb but is refuted at scale by the noun: 19 of 22 مَأْوَىٰ occurrences make it the Fire — the antithesis of a haven, indeed (32:20) a place of forced return. The only account covering all 36 is therefore the thin, polarity-neutral 'place reached as destination-abode / act of coming-to-settle', with 'protection' demoted to a frequent connotation of the verbal class alone.
Awy.strongest_counterexample: 79:39:4:2 فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ names Hellfire the maʾwā, read against its minimal pair 79:41:4:2 ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ (the Garden the maʾwā) and against 32:20:4:2 where the Fire is a maʾwā of forced return (كُلَّمَآ أَرَادُوٓا۟ أَن يَخْرُجُوا۟ مِنْهَآ أُعِيدُوا۟ فِيهَا). The identical noun denotes Hellfire and Garden alike, and denotes a locus of confinement one is forced back into: this falsifies any 'refuge/shelter/safety' nucleus and forces the root down to the valence-neutral 'place reached as destination-abode', collapsing the vivid protective verbal reading.
Awy.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B distinctiveness-weighted, C adversarial) converged on REPRESENTATIVE/MODERATE and on the punitive مَأْوَىٰ sub-class as the sole cap driver.

Tmn.candidate_root_contribution: Tmn (attested only as Form XII: iṭmaʾanna / taṭmaʾinnu / muṭmaʾinn-) = a locus (heart, soul, person, place, being) coming into or being in a settled, at-rest condition in which a prior or potential agitation — fear, doubt, or instability/precariousness — is stilled, so that the locus rests firmly, characteristically settling upon (بِ) a ground. The verb is valence-neutral: the moral color and the specific agitation removed are supplied entirely by context/subject/object, not by the root.
Tmn.plain_explanation: The word describes something that could waver, tip, or be disturbed coming to rest and holding steady. A heart stops churning with doubt or fear and settles; a person settles contentedly onto something; a town or people dwell settled and at ease; a soul is at peace. What settles it, and whether that settling is praiseworthy or blameworthy, comes from what it settles upon (God's remembrance and faith in some verses, the worldly life in others), not from the word itself.
Tmn.strongest_counterexample: 17:95:8:1 (يَمْشُونَ مُطْمَئِنِّينَ): a settledness that is not epistemic (no doubt to dispel), not cessation of any stated prior fear (angels), and not contentment-upon-a-بِ-object — it denotes a settled, at-home mode of inhabiting the earth. Folding it under the heart-reassurance nucleus requires retreat to the maximally broad gloss 'settledness,' and at that breadth Tmn's contribution stops being distinguishable from Amn (dwelling securely). This, together with 16:112's active pairing ءَامِنَةً مُّطْمَئِنَّةً (which undercuts distinctiveness from amn in the security sense), is the material resistance that caps the nucleus below STRONG.
Tmn.independent_verification: Three independent lenses read all 13 occurrences; two (B, C) independently reached MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE and C independently isolated the same outer resistant cluster and amn non-distinctiveness, corroborating the residual resistance.

jld.plain_explanation: The consonantal skeleton ج-ل-د carries two entirely separate meanings in the Quran that never meet. In nine places (all the plural noun juluwd) it means the outer skin/hide of a body: cattle-hide worked into tents (16:80), skins melted (22:20) or roasted and replaced (4:56), skins that shiver then soften beside the heart (39:23), and skins that testify against their owners alongside hearing and sight (41:20-22). In four places, all in Surah 24, it is a penal act: the imperative verb 'flog' (fa-jliduu, 24:2/24:4) together with its counted instance-noun jaldah 'one stroke' (a hundred / eighty). No flogging verse mentions skin, no skin verse mentions striking, and the two share no partner word anywhere. The only thing joining 'skin' and 'flog' is external etymology, which the source policy forbids as authority. So the honest result is not one nucleus but two unbridged classes, and the root-level claim is left unresolved.
jld.strongest_counterexample: 24:2 fa-jliduu ... mi'ata jaldatin ('flog each of them a hundred strokes') is a countable judicial act of striking with no covering in view, and it cannot be hosted by any 'skin' nucleus; conversely 16:80 juluudi al-an'aam (hide made into tents) and 39:23's juluud/quluub contrast (skin as bodily membrane) cannot be hosted by any 'striking' nucleus. The two mutually falsify any single Quran-internal nucleus: skins that melt, are replaced, and testify (22:20; 4:56:12:1; 41:20-22) share nothing textually with a counted lash. This unbridgeability is the decisive evidence for a partition rather than a unified root claim.
jld.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (bottom-up A, distinctiveness B, adversarial C) each partitioned the 13 tokens identically and each independently found no Quran-internal bridge, converging on the multi-class unresolved verdict.

rAf.candidate_root_contribution: ر ا ف names a tender, gentle inward disposition toward a personal object — a felt inclination to treat persons softly and to spare them from pain/harshness. It surfaces only as the faʿūl bearer-attribute (raʾūf) and the faʿlah quality-noun (raʾfah); it is a property of the heart (God's, the Prophet's, or believers'), object-directed (marked by bi- + human object or placed fī qulūb), not an act, gift, or guaranteed outcome, and evaluatively neutral (praised in God/Prophet, to be suppressed when it obstructs a mandated ḥadd).
rAf.plain_explanation: Across all 13 occurrences the root ر ا ف carries one idea: a soft, tender-hearted concern aimed at people. It appears as raʾūf, the one who bears that tenderness (of God 10x, of the Messenger once), and as raʾfah, the tenderness itself — placed in the hearts of Jesus's followers (57:27) or the pity that would stay the flogging hand (24:2). The quality is always directed at persons (bi-l-nās, bi-l-ʿibād, bi-kum, bi-him, bi-l-muʾminīn) and 9:128 effectively defines it: a heart pained by others' suffering and eager for their welfare. It is not the same as leniency-in-outcome (God is raʾūf while warning of Himself in 3:30 and while seizing in 16:47), and it is not always to be acted on (24:2 forbids letting it deflect God's penalty). The honest limit: in 9 of 13 tokens raʾūf/raʾfah is welded to the r-ḥ-m field (raʾūf raḥīm / raʾfatan wa-raḥmatan), and the Quran never internally states how the two differ, so a distinct semantic load beyond 'near-synonym of mercy' is only sharply shown in a minority of verses.
rAf.strongest_counterexample: 24:2:12:1 — 'وَلَا تَأْخُذْكُم بِهِمَا رَأْفَةٌ فِى دِينِ ٱللَّهِ': the sole human-subject, negated/prohibited token, positioned as an obstacle to a divine command. This is a polarity/behavioral inversion, not a semantic one: the content (a tender pull to spare the flogged from prescribed pain) is exactly the nucleus, only the evaluation is reversed. It therefore disproves any 'raʾfa = always divine / always positive / always a virtue' framing while confirming the field-level nucleus and establishing evaluative neutrality as a firm boundary.
rAf.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B family-bridge, C adversarial) converged on the same nucleus, the same 24:2 evaluative-inversion reading, and the same UNRESOLVED distinctiveness-from-rḥm verdict.

$bh.candidate_root_contribution: The root ش ب ه contributes a single thin nucleus: a GRADIENT RELATION OF LIKENESS/RESEMBLANCE holding between two or more entities (perceptual or notional), short of identity and evaluatively neutral in the root itself. The binyanim supply valence, not distinct lexical content: Form VI (تشابه / متشابه) = mutual/reciprocal resemblance; Form VIII (مشتبه) = be-resemblant (shown equivalent to VI in the same clause at 6:99); Form II (شُبِّه) = causative 'a likeness was cast/made to appear'. Confusion, deception, and interpretive ambiguity are NOT in the root: they are added compositionally by the perceiver-goal frame (عَلَى in 2:70/13:16; لِ in 4:157), by the causative binyan, or by opposition to مُحكَم (3:7).
$bh.plain_explanation: Across all 12 occurrences the root always means 'X is/becomes/is-made like Y' — never identity or equality. This is proven internally by the minimal pairs مُتَشَٰبِهًا / غَيْرَ مُتَشَٰبِهٍ (6:141, 6:99), where likeness is explicitly gradable and negatable, and by 6:99 pairing Form VIII (مُشْتَبِهًا) with Form VI (غَيْرَ مُتَشَٰبِهٍ) as one meaning. The famous 'confusion/ambiguity/deception' readings arise only when the surface adds a burdened observer (تشابه + عَلَى → 'became indistinguishable to them', 2:70/13:16), a causing agent (Form II شُبِّه, 4:157), or the muḥkam contrast (3:7). The account is capped below STRONG because one Form-VI lexeme carries logically incompatible senses for the same referent-domain: the WHOLE Book is praised as مُّتَشَٰبِهًا 'self-consistent' (39:23) while only SOME verses are مُتَشَٰبِهَٰت 'ambiguous', opposed to مُّحْكَمَٰت and tied to fitna (3:7). That 'ambiguous-scripture' specialization is a lexicalized sub-class not derivable from bare 'resemblance', and the causative deceptive شُبِّه (4:157) is singly attested.
$bh.strongest_counterexample: The intra-lexeme collision 3:7 vs 39:23: the SAME Form VI participle مُتَشَٰبِه is predicated of the WHOLE Book as praise (self-consistent/harmonious, كِتَٰبًا مُّتَشَٰبِهًا مَّثَانِيَ, 39:23) yet of only SOME verses opposed to مُّحْكَمَٰت and tied to ٱبْتِغَآءَ ٱلْفِتْنَةِ (وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَٰبِهَٰتٌ … مَا تَشَٰبَهَ مِنْهُ, 3:7); the 'undecidable/ambiguous' sense is not derivable from 'resemblance' without importing the muḥkam contrast, and the 'consistent' vs 'ambiguous' senses are incompatible on quantity and sense and are NOT bridged Quran-internally. Secondary counterexample: 4:157 شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ, the lone Form II, a caused impersonal deceptive semblance whose 'counterfeit/substitute' force cannot be excluded at n=1.
$bh.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B independent, C adversarial) converged on one likeness nucleus with the same two capping factors (3:7 lexicalized class; 4:157 singleton causative).

Esr.candidate_root_contribution: ع س ر marks the adverse pole of a Quran-internal ease/difficulty axis: the condition or quality of being hard-going, difficult to do, bear, or afford — the marked, dispreferred antonym of يُسْر/مَيْسَرَة (ease). Across its derivational family the nucleus is packaged as an abstract mass-noun (عُسْر), a concrete circumstance of straitened means (عُسْرَة), a lexicalized hard course/destiny (عُسْرَى), an adjective 'hard-to-undergo' fixed to the Day (عَسِير/عَسِر), and a reciprocal verb of mutual impasse (تَعَاسَرَ). The distinctive shading beyond bare 'not-easy' — burdensome constraint borne against capacity, relievable, and party-relative — is representative but leans partly on co-text, so it is not generalized to full root strength.
Esr.plain_explanation: The root ع س ر is the Quran's word-family for hardship and difficulty. Its meaning is anchored by the text itself, which repeatedly pairs it with its opposite يُسْر (ease): God wills ease for you and not hardship (2:185), after hardship comes ease (65:7), with hardship is ease (94:5-6), and a debtor in hardship waits for ease of means (2:280). It covers abstract hardship, financial straitness, a hard Day of Judgment, a hard destiny, and two people making things mutually difficult. It is never permanent, never something God endorses, and it is relative to who bears it.
Esr.strongest_counterexample: 92:10:2:3 «فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ» — the verb نُيَسِّر (to ease/facilitate, root ي س ر) takes ٱلْعُسْرَىٰ (hardship) as its goal: 'We will ease him toward hardship.' On a naive reading of عسر as simply 'the opposite of ease,' easing-toward-hardship is self-contradictory, placing the two anchoring antonyms in one clause. It survives only because ٱلْعُسْرَىٰ is here lexicalized as a substantive 'the hard course/destiny' (mirroring ٱلْيُسْرَىٰ at 92:7), with يسّر operating on the manner of arrival, not the destination. It does not disprove the nucleus but exposes that the elative form is partly lexicalized and that the yusr-antonymy is a systemic pairing rather than a live compositional negation.
Esr.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) all located the same yusr/maysara antonym bridge across 2:185, 2:280, 65:7, 92:7↔10, 94:5-6; two of three independently capped at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE citing the same thin-distinctiveness and Form-VI-singleton grounds.

Srm.candidate_root_contribution: Agentive forcible severing / cutting-off of a plant's produce or growth — i.e. reaping or plucking a garden's yield off the plant. Attested only as a derivational family (imperfect verb + active participle for the agentive act) within the single al-Qalam garden-owners episode; the sole nominal token (faʿīl ṣarīm) coheres as the resultative 'cut-off/stripped' face but is not Quran-internally demonstrated as such.
Srm.plain_explanation: In all three occurrences ص ر م sits inside one story (Sūrat al-Qalam 68:17-22, the garden owners). Two tokens are productive and agentive: the verb la-yaṣrimunna-hā (68:17, 'they swore they would surely ṣrm the garden at daybreak') and the active participle ṣārimīn (68:22, 'go early to your crop if you are ṣārimīn / reapers'), both bound to agricultural objects (the garden, the ḥarth). These fix the sense as 'cut the produce off the plant' = reap/strip. The third token is the noun ṣarīm (68:20, 'so by morning it became ka-l-ṣarīm'), where the garden is the patient after being struck by a ṭāʾif. Read as the resultative/patient face of the same nucleus ('a thing cut off / stripped bare') it completes an elegant agent-action-result irony, but it is a non-recurring nominal whose sense rests on narrative inference rather than internal triangulation, so the account is held at MODERATE and to this derivational family only.
Srm.strongest_counterexample: 68:20 ka-l-ṣarīm resists the agentive 'reap/cut produce' account: the garden was not reaped but devastated by a ṭāʾif, yet it is called ṣarīm. faʿīl is voice-ambiguous (active 'that which cuts' vs. resultative 'that which is cut off'), the noun is non-recurring so its sense cannot be triangulated internally, and the destruction is carried by a separate root — so assigning it the 'stripped/cut-off' resultative sense is narrative inference, not lexical demonstration. It shows 'harvest' alone is too narrow and prevents a fully demonstrated single nucleus, capping strength at MODERATE.
Srm.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each read all 3/3 occurrences and independently converged on REPRESENTATIVE/MODERATE with ṣarīm (68:20) flagged as the resistant token; adversary C additionally logged that a unified-nucleus claim over all three is internally irrefutable.

bhj.candidate_root_contribution: bhj marks a positive, manifest, evaluative quality of vegetation freshly brought forth by God from otherwise dead/barren earth via sent-down water — the pleasing, flourishing character of the grown plant-cover (pairs/kinds, orchards), foregrounded as visually-apprehended sign material. It is a stative quality of the product, complementary to (not synonymous with) the act of growing (nbt). The precise semantic core is left under-determined between aesthetic splendor and vital lushness, which internal evidence cannot adjudicate.
bhj.plain_explanation: In all three Quranic occurrences the root bhj describes plants that God causes to grow after rain revives the earth. As the adjective bahiyj it qualifies 'every kind/pair' of vegetation (22:5, 50:7); as the noun bahjah it is the quality that gardens 'possess' (27:60). Across all three it names the attractive, thriving quality of divinely-grown vegetation, presented as a sign of God's power and of resurrection. The evidence does not settle whether the quality is essentially beauty/splendor or lushness/vitality, and the root is never applied to anything outside grown vegetation.
bhj.strongest_counterexample: 27:60 (hadaaʾiq dhaata bahjatin) applies bhj to mature, established orchards where the emergence-from-deadness element is absent. This disproves an over-narrow 'vitality-of-revival' reading licensed by 22:5's hamidah→ihtazzat→rabat chain, forcing the broader appearance/quality account — but it does not create a resistant class; it narrows the claim. Conversely, 22:5's vitality verbs (ihtazzat, rabat) pull against a purely aesthetic gloss. Neither breaks the nucleus; together they show the core is genuinely under-determined between aesthetic-splendor and vital-lushness.
bhj.independent_verification: All three lenses (A, B, adversary C) independently read 3/3 occurrences in full and converged on one un-resisted nucleus with the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grading and the same aesthetic-vs-vital under-determination.

frt.candidate_root_contribution: An attribute of water meaning fresh/sweet and fit-to-drink — the positive potable pole of water, standing in explicit binary opposition to briny-bitter water (milḥ ujāj). Attested only as the adjective furāt; the root has no verbal or distinct nominal footprint.
frt.plain_explanation: Every one of the 3 occurrences of frt is the same adjective furāt qualifying water. Twice (25:53, 35:12) it appears as the second predicate of the 'sweet' sea (ʿadhbun furātun) set against the salt-bitter sea (milḥun ujājun); once (77:27) it stands alone as the sole quality of the water God gives people to drink (māʾan furātan). Across all three, furāt marks water as fresh and drinkable — the opposite of undrinkable briny water. Whether furāt adds a specific nuance beyond ʿadhb (sweet) cannot be settled from the Quran alone, since the two are only ever co-predicated (25:53, 35:12) and the one solo use (77:27) shows furāt can carry the 'good drinking water' sense by itself but does not isolate its differential content.
frt.strongest_counterexample: None survives against the core sense: there is no occurrence where furāt attaches to non-potable, salty, or non-water referents, nor any with negative valence — the corpus is adversarially clean on 'fresh/drinkable water'. The residual weakness is precision, not consistency: in 25:53 and 35:12 furāt is co-predicated with ʿadhb, so it cannot be decisively separated from a mere near-synonym/emphatic doublet of ʿadhb; only the solo use in 77:27 pushes back by showing furāt can carry the sense alone, but 3 tokens in essentially one collocational frame cannot fix furāt's distinct differential content.
frt.independent_verification: Cross-checked against Lens A, Lens B, and Adversary C — all three independently reached the same single-class, MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE verdict and all three flagged the ʿadhb-vs-furāt distinctiveness as the sole unresolved point; packet word_refs, forms (ADJ), and verse_text confirmed directly against frt.json.

hmz.candidate_root_contribution: A hostile, pejorative jab/prod directed at a target so as to wound or unsettle it. In the dominant and best-anchored realization (the intensive human-agent forms humazah/hammaz) this is habitual verbal disparagement/defamation of other persons; the one act-noun realization (hamazat) is the devils' goadings/promptings directed at the seeker's own soul. The narrow human sub-sense is well-supported; the cross-class 'directed hostile prod' nucleus that also covers 23:97 is defensible but thin (rests on abstraction, n=1 on the satanic side).
hmz.plain_explanation: hmz never appears as a finite verb; all three tokens are nominal/adjectival. Two of them are intensive agent forms describing a kind of person: humazah (104:1, paired with lumazah under 'woe') and hammaz (68:11, in a vice-list next to namim/talebearing). Both name one who habitually jabs at and disparages other people. The third, hamazat al-shayatin (23:97), is a plural act-noun for the devils' promptings that a person seeks refuge from. Across all three the sense is uniformly hostile and blameworthy; the divergence is that the devils' hamazat target the seeker himself rather than a third party's reputation, which the narrow human sense does not cover.
hmz.strongest_counterexample: 23:97 (hamazat al-shayatin) resists the dominant, best-attested sense 'habitual disparagement/defamation of other people' carried by the two morphologically parallel human-agent forms: the agent is devils not humans, the medium is not demonstrably verbal, and the target is the seeker's own soul rather than a third party's reputation. It fits only the thinner abstract nucleus 'hostile directed prod at a target,' which is reached by abstraction rather than by any Quran-internal bridge (no verse shows a devil defaming, nor a human hamz in a non-defamation sense).
hmz.independent_verification: Three independent analyses (A bottom-up, B lens, C adversarial) each converged on MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE with 23:97 as the resistant seam.

jyb.candidate_root_contribution: jayb denotes a concrete garment feature: the opening/slit of clothing at the neck and breast (the bosom-aperture) — that into which a hand is inserted (فِى) and over which a covering is drawn (عَلَىٰ). Attested only as a noun, in singular (جَيْب) and plural (جُيُوب); no verbal, abstract, or metaphorical extension.
jyb.plain_explanation: Across all three occurrences جيب names the chest-level opening of a worn garment — the front slit through which the head/neck passes, into which Moses inserts his hand (27:12, 28:32) and over which women draw their head-coverings (24:31). It is the garment's aperture, not the body it exposes and not the cloth that covers it. The singular/plural difference is purely referential (one man's garment vs many women's garments), not a shift in meaning.
jyb.strongest_counterexample: 24:31:18:1 (جُيُوبِهِنَّ) is the sole token outside the near-verbatim Moses doublet: it is plural, in a legal (not miracle) register, and it carries the entire cross-class bridge from 'aperture a hand is inserted into' (فِى, 27:12/28:32) to 'opening a covering is drawn over' (عَلَىٰ). It also admits a rival referent — nothing Quran-internal forces juyūb to mean the cloth-aperture rather than the bodily bosom it exposes — so the whole unity claim rests on this one under-attested, mildly ambiguous verse. It does not contradict the nucleus (same physical locus, both frames satisfied by one garment opening), so it is an adversarial boundary and breadth limit, not a resistant sub-class.
jyb.independent_verification: Three independent analyses (Lens A bottom-up, Lens B contrastive, Lens C adversarial) converged on the same garment-aperture nucleus, agreed there is no resistant sub-class, and independently identified 24:31 as the sole breadth wedge — none produced a failing occurrence.

smw.plain_explanation: The root smw appears 381 times and splits, with an exhaustive and clean morphological break, into two macro-fields that never once meet inside a verse. (A) The sky-stem samaa'/samaawaat (310) means the elevated created expanse above the earth: a built vault, the direction and source of what descends, and the upper term of the 'heavens-and-earth' totality. (B) The name-stem family (71) — ism/asmaa' (the borne/invoked designation), sammaa/tasmiyah (the act of naming), samiyy (namesake), musammaa (the lexicalized 'appointed term') — means a verbal designation attached to a referent, a label that may be true, empty, or even base. Nothing in the Quran bridges the two: no verse uses a sky-word to mean 'name' or a name-word to mean 'sky', no form-I 'to be high/ascend' verb of this root exists (height is always carried by other roots), and the one morphological bridge-candidate (samiyy, faEiyl) resolves inside the name-family as 'namesake' (19:7). The tempting single etymon 'elevation/height' is diachronic Arabic lexicography, forbidden here as authority, and is affirmatively disconfirmed internally (87:1 delegates highness to ʿlw, not to smw; idol-names are authority-less; ajal musammaa is a fixed due-date). The honest Quran-internal result is therefore not one nucleus but two coherent, unbridged classes.
smw.strongest_counterexample: إِنْ هِىَ إِلَّآ أَسْمَآءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَٰنٍ (53:23; also 7:71, 12:40) — a name is nothing but an empty, authority-less human token — set against أَمِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ بَنَىٰهَا (79:27; 51:47, 21:32), where samaa' is the mightiest God-built physical reality. No contentful nucleus can span 'empty man-made word' and 'God-constructed firmament' without collapsing into vacuity; and where the text does pair a name with highness (87:1 ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلْأَعْلَى) the highness is carried by a different root (ʿlw) on the Lord, not by smw on the name. This falsifies any 'elevation' bridge as a Quran-internal semantic (as opposed to historical) claim.
smw.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on the same exhaustive 2-macro-class partition and the same non-unity conclusion, and each independently rejected the 'elevation' etymon on Quran-internal grounds.

rAy.candidate_root_contribution: rAy encodes the coming of something into a percipient's apprehension — prototypically by sight, and modality-/truth-neutral (the perceived may be false, in a dream, or a non-visible fact). This single perceptual nucleus is transformed by regular, Quran-internally attested derivation: Form IV = cause-to-perceive / make-visible (show), Form VI = come into mutual sight, Form I with a predicative complement = 'regard/deem X as Y', and the nominals name the perceived-content in a modality (ru'ya = dream/vision, ra'y = settled view, ri'y = outward appearance, ra'ya l-'ayn = eye-perception). Two derivationally-bridged but semantically lexicalized sub-classes fall outside a bare perceptual gloss and cap the account: the frozen deictic interrogative a-ra'ayta(ka)/a-fa-ra'aytum ('tell me / consider / suppose'), in which the perceptual content is bleached, and Form III ri'a'/yura'una ('ostentation, doing-to-be-seen'), a moral-pragmatic specialization.
rAy.plain_explanation: At its core the root means 'to have something become present/evident to you' — usually by seeing it with the eyes, but the same verb runs smoothly into 'realize', 'find/consider so', and 'see in a dream'. The system is regular: Form IV is 'show' (make someone see), Form VI is 'see one another', and the nouns name what is seen (a dream, an opinion, an outward look). Two offshoots have drifted into fixed meanings the plain 'perceive' does not predict: the frozen question-opener a-ra'ayta ('tell me / what do you think if...'), where nothing is actually being seen, and ri'a' ('showing off to be seen by people'). Because those two coherent sub-classes resist the bare 'perceive' account, the claim is graded MODERATE and REPRESENTATIVE rather than universal.
rAy.strongest_counterexample: The frozen deictic idiom a-ra'aytaka(um) / a-fa-ra'aytum, most sharply at 6:40:2:2 (qul a-ra'aytakum in atakum 'adhabu llah ... a-ghayra llahi tad'un), 6:47:2:2 and 17:62:2:2 (qala a-ra'aytaka hadha lladhi karramta 'alayya). Here the perceptual content is fully bleached, the morphology is fossilized (the -ka/-kum is a frozen non-argument, invariant to sense), and the verb functions as a discourse operator 'tell me / consider / suppose' governing a conditional plus an unrelated interrogative — nothing is seen. With its 33 idiom-siblings this is the coherent resistant sub-class that blocks any STRONG/UNIVERSAL 'ra'a = perceive' claim. Secondarily, the ri'a'/yura'una ostentation class (2:264:12:1, 4:38:4:1, 8:47:8:2, 4:142:13:1, 107:6:3:1) carries a moral 'hypocritical display' surplus not recoverable from 'perceive/be-seen'.
rAy.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A/B/C) converged on the same nucleus, the same two resistant sub-classes, and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade; word_refs, forms, and the 328/237/34/40/2/5/10 partition were re-confirmed directly against the packet.

bED.candidate_root_contribution: baED is a relational partitive nominal designating an unspecified PROPER (non-total) PART / SUBSET of an identified whole - 'some of / a portion of / one of (several)' - that presupposes a larger whole, stands complementary to a remainder, and is inherently less than the totality (kull). Quantity and identity of the portion are left indeterminate; the whole may be a mass, an abstract, a time-span, a scripture, produce, or an enumerable plurality. Its reciprocal / distributive reading ('one another', 'some ... others') is compositional doubling of the same partitive across a predicate, not a second lexical sense.
bED.plain_explanation: In 157 of 158 occurrences baED means 'part of / some of / one of' a stated whole - always less than all, with the size and which-member left vague. When it is repeated (baED ... baED) it simply splits one whole into two interacting portions, and the surrounding verb (favour, enmity, alliance, whispering, wronging) supplies the relation; baED itself only ever contributes 'a portion of'. The single remaining token, baEuwDap 'a gnat' at 2:26, is a concrete creature-name that shares only the consonantal skeleton and carries no partitive meaning, so it is treated as a separate lexeme and is not folded into the claim.
bED.strongest_counterexample: At 2:26:9:1 baEuwDapF (baEuwDap, 'a gnat') is a concrete count-noun of a different morphological pattern (faEuwlap, feminine, taa marbuutap + tanwiin, medial waaw) naming a whole creature used as the object of yaDrib maθalan and scaled against famaa fawqahaa; it exhibits zero partitive/subset function and presupposes no whole, so no Quran-internal bridge links it to the baED partitive nucleus.
bED.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each read all 158 occurrences and converged on the same nucleus, the same compositional analysis of doubling, and the same single unbridged outlier.

rwd.candidate_root_contribution: Purposive orientation toward an as-yet-unrealized outcome — a subject being set/directed toward a state of affairs it aims to bring about. In the dominant Form IV (arāda/yurīdu, 139 occ.) this surfaces as 'to will / intend / purpose / direct oneself (or be directed) toward' an aim; it names the directedness, not its achievement, and is neutral both affectively (not 'desire/liking') and morally (valence sits in the complement). Form III (rāwada, 8 occ.) is a lexicalized interpersonal-intensive derivative of this orientation ('press/solicit a resistant person, ʿan their nafs/withheld thing, to yield'), and the isolated adverb ruwaydan (1 occ., 'gently/a little') is an unbridged lexicalized item — so the account is a derivational family, not a single root-wide meaning.
rwd.plain_explanation: The root rwd shows up in the Quran as three morphological classes with no attested base verb (form I never occurs). The big class, Form IV yurīdu/arāda, means to set one's will/aim on an outcome: God 'intends ease for you' (2:185), people 'want the world' (3:152), even a wall 'is about to / tends to' collapse (18:77) — so it is directedness toward a goal, not conscious desire, and not the goal's accomplishment (many intentions are frustrated). Form III rāwada is a different, narrow scene-word: to keep pressing a person to give up what they withhold, against resistance (Yusuf held firm, 12:32; Lot's guests, 54:37). And ruwaydan (86:17) is just an adverb 'gently/a little', with nothing to do with willing or soliciting. The three connect only through an unattested base sense, so the honest result is a family with a strong Form IV core, a bridged-but-lexicalized Form III branch, and one unbridged adverb — moderate, representative, not universal.
rwd.strongest_counterexample: 86:17 ruwaydan (fa-mahhili l-kāfirīna amhilhum ruwaydan) is a frozen manner/degree adverb 'gently / a little (while)' modifying the granting of respite; it carries no volitional, purposive, or interpersonal content and is connected to the willing/soliciting senses by no Quran-internal bridge (the only link, base form I rāda, never occurs), so it defeats any single-nucleus/UNIVERSAL claim for the root.
rwd.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (bottom-up, independent, adversary) converged on MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE derivational-family with ruwaydan unbridged and Form III lexicalized; packet counts (139/8/1=148) and all cited word_refs verified against rwd.json.

n*r.candidate_root_contribution: Across its warning derivational family (Form IV verb 'andhara/yun*iru', the participles mun*ir/mun*ar, the fa'iyl agent-noun na*iyr, its plural nu*ur and masdar nu*or), n*r contributes: the agentive advance delivery of NOTICE that a grave/adverse consequence is impending, so the recipient may take heed. It is other-directed (agent -> recipient), forward-looking (before the event), fixed to the negative pole (systematic antonym of bashiyr 'glad tidings'), and does not entail uptake, belief, or the consequence itself. This is REPRESENTATIVE, not the whole root: a small, morphologically distinct, lexicalized VOW class (Form I na*aro + noun na*r/nu*uwr) is co-attested but Quran-internally UNBRIDGED to warning and resists this account.
n*r.plain_explanation: The root n*r overwhelmingly (124/130) means to WARN: an authorised agent (God, messenger, prophet, even jinn) puts heedless people on notice of a coming adverse outcome (a punishment, a fire, a dreaded Day) so they may take heed. This warning sense is broad, morphologically rich, and pinned down by its constant contrast with 'good tidings' (bashiyr). Separately, a small cluster of 6 occurrences uses the same consonants to mean a VOW: a person binds themselves by a pledge to God (a fast, an unborn child, an offering) which is then to be fulfilled. The direction (human->God), the valence (pious self-dedication, not threat), and the collocation (fulfilment, wafaa') are all opposite to warning, and no verse bridges the two. So the root's representative contribution is WARN, with VOW recorded as a genuine resistant lexicalized class rather than forced into unity.
n*r.strongest_counterexample: The plural skeleton collides across the two classes with irreconcilable meanings: 22:29:5:1 'wa-l-yuufuu nu*uwra-hum' (let them FULFILL their VOWS) vs the identical consonantal plural at 54:5:5:2 'fa-maa tughni l-nu*uru' (the WARNINGS availed nothing) and 10:101:10:3. Same triliteral, same plural skeleton, two unbridged senses (personal binding obligations vs God's cautionary announcements). The Form-I verb is equally decisive: 19:26:12:1 'innii na*artu li-l-rahmaani sawman' (I have VOWED a fast to the Most Merciful) and 3:35:7:1 'na*artu laka maa fii batnii' (I have VOWED to You what is in my womb) cannot be read as putting anyone on notice of a threat, against warn-verb tokens such as 92:14:1:2 'fa-an*artu-kum naaran talazzaa' (I have WARNED you of a blazing fire). No occurrence sits astride the two senses.
n*r.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each achieved full 130/130 coverage and independently reached the same warn/vow partition with no Quran-internal bridge; the aggregator re-opened the packet and confirmed the vow word_refs, forms (V/N, verb_form None), and the 22:29 vs 54:5 plural surface collision.

sxr.plain_explanation: The 42 occurrences of س خ ر do not resolve to a single Quran-internal nucleus. They fall into two large, internally coherent classes in strict complementary distribution, with no verse that bridges them. Class A (derision): Form I verbs, the one Form X verb, and the derision nouns سِخْرِيّ/ٱلسَّٰخِرِين — an attitudinal/speech act aimed at a PERSON, governing its target with مِن ('mock AT'), e.g. سَخِرُوا۟ مِنْهُ (11:38), يَسْخَرُونَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ (2:212), لَا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ (49:11); it never takes a لـ-beneficiary or a cosmic patient and effects no change in the target. Class B (subjection): all Form II (verb, both passive participles مُسَخَّرَٰت/ٱلْمُسَخَّر) plus the noun سُخْرِيّ (43:32) — a causative deployment act that places a (usually inanimate, cosmic) thing under command to run to a purpose, governing with لـ (لَكُمُ ٱلْفُلْكَ), a direct accusative (ٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ), or once عَلَى (69:7 against ʿĀd), collocated with بِأَمْرِهِ and يَجْرِى لِأَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى. No Form I ever means 'subject' and no Form II ever means 'mock'; the two syntactic frames (مِن vs لـ/عَلَى/acc) never overlap. Because the two senses are not Quran-internally bridged, the honest result is a partition into classes, not one nucleus.
sxr.strongest_counterexample: The near-minimal vowel pair on one consonantal skeleton س-خ-ر-ي: سِخْرِيّ (kasra: sixoriy~FA) at 23:110 and 38:63 = object of DERISION (Class A), versus سُخْرِيّ (damma: suxoriy~FA) at 43:32 = object of SERVICE/subordination (Class B). Identical bare-noun morphology (qac_pos=N, qac_verb_form=null in all three), distinguished only by the first vowel and used in the two opposite senses with no bridging context. That the language must change the vowel to keep the two nouns apart is Quran-internal evidence of two lexemes on one skeleton, not one meaning with contextual shading — a single nucleus would not need a vocalic minimal pair to disambiguate itself.
sxr.independent_verification: All three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) converged on the same two-class partition with no Quran-internal bridge and identified 43:32 as the pivot, corroborating the UNRESOLVED unity verdict.

$Er.candidate_root_contribution: In its verbal derivational family (Form I ya$oEuru/ta$oEuru + Form IV causative yu$oEiru), the root denotes low-threshold apprehension: to sense/notice/register a real but non-obvious state below the level of deliberate knowledge; Form IV = to cause such perception. This account covers 27/40 occurrences and does NOT extend, on any Quran-internal bridge, to the nominal/onomastic classes (hair, poet/poetry, ritual waymarks, the star Sirius).
$Er.plain_explanation: The 40 occurrences do not share one meaning. There is one strong, internally clean verbal sense: 'to perceive/notice/be aware of' something subtle or hidden. Strikingly, all 27 verbal tokens appear only under negation, prohibition, or counterfactual (laA/wamaA ya$oEuruwn; law ta$oEuruwn 26:113; walaA yu$oEiranna 18:19; wamaA yu$oEirukum 6:109) - the Quran names this faculty only at its point of failure and never affirms successful perception. Alongside this verb sit four lexicalized noun/name classes that share only the consonants $-E-r: >a$oEaAr = animal hair (16:80), $aAEir/$uEaraA'/$iEr = poet/poetry (a polemical slur, contrasted with revelation in 36:69), $aEaA}ir/al-ma$oEar = consecrated ritual markers/waymark (2:158, 2:198, 5:2, 22:32, 22:36), and al-$iEraY = the star Sirius (53:49). No verse links any of these to 'perceive'. Because these classes resist the verbal sense and no Quran-internal bridge unites them, the honest result is multi-class: a representative verbal account, not a single root meaning.
$Er.strongest_counterexample: 16:80:21:2 - wa>a$oEaArihaA >avaAvFA wamataAEFA: >a$oEaAr is concrete animal HAIR, coordinated with wool (>aSowaAf) and fur (>awobaAr) as raw material for furnishings. It has zero awareness/perception content and cannot be generated from 'perceive' - nor 'perceive' from it - without an external etymological bridge the source policy forbids. This single occurrence falsifies any claim that one nucleus spans all 40 tokens (53:49 al-$iEraY, the star, is a second such homonym).
$Er.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each reached MULTI-CLASS / MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE with the same verbal nucleus and the same unbridged nominal classes; adversary C endorsed the homonym-cluster account as stronger than any unified nucleus.

slT.candidate_root_contribution: slT contributes CONFERRED, LEGITIMATING POWER-TO-PREVAIL: a granted authorizing ground by which one is entitled or empowered to prevail — realized as (a) an authorizing/probative warrant FOR a claim or mission, and (b) sanctioned authority/dominance OVER persons (the Form II verb being the causative 'set/confer such authority over'). Its distinctive, narrow feature is that it is characteristically bestowed from outside (anzala/nazzala, jaʿala, ātā, sallaṭa) and relational (predicated with ʿalā persons, or bi-/li- a claim), never intrinsic self-generated force.
slT.plain_explanation: The root surfaces overwhelmingly as one noun, sulṭān (37 of 39), plus a causative verb sallaṭa/yusalliṭu (2). Two large usages recur: a warrant/mandate that authorizes a claim or mission (usually 'clear', 'sent down', or 'brought' — e.g. Moses given a sulṭān mubīn; no sulṭān sent down for idols) and an authority/hold over persons (Satan disclaiming or scoping his sulṭān; God setting parties over one another). The Quran itself joins these two directions at 4:91, 4:144, and 17:33, where the warrant-marker mubīn/right sits on an over-persons sulṭān — so they read as two applications of one 'granted power-to-prevail', not two unrelated homonyms. But the account is not adversarially clean: 55:33 uses sulṭān as bare enabling means, and 69:29 as a possessed dominion that simply perished, neither of which reduces cleanly to warrant-or-authority-over. Hence a supported but capped, representative judgment.
slT.strongest_counterexample: 55:33 (yā-maʿshara l-jinni wa-l-insi ... lā tanfudhūna illā bi-sulṭānin): here sulṭān is sheer enabling means/capacity to penetrate the cosmic regions, with no adversary to dominate and no claim to warrant; it fits only the most abstract 'authorization' and thins the distinctive granted-relational-legitimating profile to raw capability, exposing the risk that a single unifying gloss ('authority') becomes a vague abstraction that fits everything.
slT.independent_verification: Packet re-opened and all 39 word_refs, forms (N=37, V(II)=2), and verse_texts confirmed against sl_54_.json; cluster counts (23+7+3+2+2+2) sum to 39.

qrr.candidate_root_contribution: Coming to, or being kept in, a settled/stationary/enduring state at a locus or point — hence a fixed place of rest (abode, lodging) and, by internal extension, a fixed/appointed terminus in time. Value-neutral (applied to Paradise and Hell alike) and defined against motion/transience/deposit; this fixity account governs the derivational family N qaraar, N(X) mustaqarr/mustaqirr, V(I) qarna, V(IV) causative nuqirru, and V(X) istaqarra, but does NOT govern the whole root.
qrr.plain_explanation: Across most of its forms qrr denotes settledness: a thing coming to rest and staying fixed in a place or condition. The finite verbs anchor it literally — the mountain that would 'stay put in its place' (istaqarra, 7:143), the command to 'remain settled in your houses' (qarna, 33:33), and God 'causing to lodge/settle in the wombs what He wills' (nuqirru, 22:5). From this the nouns follow: the earth 'made a stable footing' (qaraaran, 27:61/40:64), the womb as a 'firm lodging' (qaraarin makiin, 23:13/77:21), earthly and eschatological 'abodes' (mustaqarr; daar al-qaraar). Fixity in place shades internally into a fixed appointed point (the sun running 'to a settling-point for it', 36:38; 'for every tiding a settled point', 6:67; the final 'settled destination to your Lord', 75:12). The negative case is diagnostic: the uprooted evil tree 'has no qaraar' (14:26) = no fixed footing. But the root is not one meaning: 'affirm/acknowledge a covenant' (aqrartum, 2:84; 3:81) is a bleached speech-act, the qurrat-ʿayn 'eye-comfort' idiom is locked to ʿayn and paired with 'not grieving', and qawaariir 'glass/crystal' carries no fixity content at all.
qrr.strongest_counterexample: 27:44:17:1 — 'sarhun mumarradun min qawaariira' (a smoothed palace-floor of glass/crystal, which Bilqis mistook for a pool of water). The textually-salient properties are transparency and smoothness, wholly orthogonal to fixity/rest/settledness, with no Quran-internal thread linking 'glass' to the nucleus. Unlike the 76:15-16 vessels, the floor admits no 'container' rationalization. This concrete nominal shares only the consonantal skeleton and decisively defeats any UNIVERSAL/single-nucleus whole-root claim (same root != one meaning).
qrr.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversarial C) converged on the same partition and the same REPRESENTATIVE/MODERATE grade; adversary C additionally failed to break the nucleus internally while confirming qawaariir as the decisive counterexample.

Hdv.candidate_root_contribution: In its nominal (Hadiyv-/>aHaAdiyv-) and Form-II (Had~ava) family, root Hdv contributes: a unit of communicated discourse — an account/report/statement/tidings, i.e. the told-content about a subject (including the revealed discourse) — and, in Form II, the act of conveying such a discourse to a hearer. The contribution is truth-neutral, novelty-neutral, register-neutral and medium-neutral: value comes from context, not from the root. This family-scoped claim deliberately EXCLUDES the Form-IV family (>aHodava / muHodav), whose sense is origination/bringing-newly-into-being and which is NOT Quran-internally bridged to the discourse sense.
Hdv.plain_explanation: Across 31 of 36 occurrences the root names 'a piece of what is said/told' — an account, report, statement or tidings (the noun HadiyT) and, as a verb (Form II), 'to tell/recount it to someone.' It covers the account of Moses, the guests of Abraham, the best discourse (the Book), idle talk, a confided secret, a fabricated account and the most truthful speech alike. A separate 5-occurrence Form-IV family (>uHodiTa/yuHodiTu 'bring newly into being' and muHodaT 'freshly produced') means origination, not telling, and even brings forth a non-verbal 'affair' (>amr, 65:1). The Quran never uses Form IV to mean 'narrate' nor the noun to mean 'a newly-made thing', so the two families are reported as distinct and the unifying 'newness/coming-to-be' idea is left unresolved rather than forced.
Hdv.strongest_counterexample: 65:1:38:1 — laEal~a All~aha yuHodiTu baEoda *aalika >amoraF ('perhaps Allah will bring about after that a matter'): the thing brought newly into being is an >amr (a non-verbal affair/decree), carrying zero communicative content. This falsifies any attempt to unify the whole root under a communicative 'discourse/account' nucleus and, together with the discourse family's indifference to newness, blocks a single root-level nucleus — forcing the origination family to be reported as an unbridged, resistant class.
Hdv.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A semantic-segregation, B derivational-unity/neighbour-distinctiveness, C adversarial) converged on the same morphology-meaning split and the same 65:1 wedge; the aggregator re-opened the packet and confirmed every word_ref, form (N=28/N(IV)=2/V(II)=3/V(IV)=3) and object (*ikor vs >amr vs >axobaAr).

bgt.candidate_root_contribution: بَغْتَةً marks the onset/arrival of a decreed, dreaded event (the Hour ٱلسَّاعَة, the punishment ٱلْعَذَاب, or God's seizing أخذ) in a manner experienced by its recipients as unperceived and unprepared-for — arriving unheralded *to them*, Quran-internally opposed to جَهْرَةً (open/manifest arrival, 6:47). The distinctive axis is perceptibility-of-onset to the victim (hidden vs. open), not lexicalized velocity; the destructive/eschatological content is carried by the subject-nouns, not by بغت. The entire root footprint is this one frozen accusative adverb.
bgt.plain_explanation: Every one of the 13 occurrences is the identical word بَغْتَةً — an accusative adverb ('baghtatan') attached to a verb of coming (تأتي/يأتي/جاء/أتى) or of God's seizing (أخذنٰهم). There is no verb, participle, or other noun form of this root anywhere in the corpus, so we can only certify the behavior of one lexicalized adverb, not a root paradigm. The word says the Hour or the punishment reaches people while they do not perceive it and cannot prepare or repel it: six verses gloss it directly with وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ / وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَشْعُرُونَ, 21:40 says it dumbfounds them (فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ) so they cannot repel it, and 6:47 sets it explicitly against جَهْرَةً ('openly'), showing the contrast is about being unperceived, not about being fast. It never modifies a neutral or welcome arrival.
bgt.strongest_counterexample: 47:18:7:1 «أَن تَأْتِيَهُم بَغْتَةً فَقَدْ جَآءَ أَشْرَاطُهَا» — its portents have already come, yet the arrival is still بَغْتَةً. This defeats any maximal 'no warning / utterly unforeseeable' reading and disciplines the claim down to the narrow recipient-non-perception sense: signs may be present ambiently, but the actual onset still catches them unapprehended and unprepared. It refines the nucleus rather than breaking it.
bgt.independent_verification: Three independent analysts (A, B, C) each read all 13 tokens; all affirm the narrow account fits every occurrence with no resistant sub-class, converging on the perceptibility-of-onset distinctive (B at STRONG, A and C at MODERATE).

jwr.plain_explanation: Across all 13 occurrences the root ج و ر does not present one Quran-internal meaning. The data partitions cleanly by derivational form into three lexicalized senses: (1) spatial adjacency / dwelling-alongside — form III yujaAwiru (33:60), the form-VI participle mutajaAwiraAt (13:4, inanimate tracts of land), and the noun jaAr as 'neighbor' (4:36 twice); (2) granting/seeking refuge FROM a named threat — every form IV and the single form X (9:6 istajaAra + >ajir; 23:88 yujiyr / yujaAr; 46:31, 67:28, 72:22, all with min [threat]), plus the noun jaAr as 'protector/guarantor' (8:48, Satan); (3) deviation from the straight way — the form-I participle jaA}ir (16:9), set against qaSd al-sabiyl. The only thing linking senses (1) and (2) is the single noun jaAr reading two ways, and the only account that would also absorb (3) is a vague 'to one's side' abstraction that predicts nothing distinctive. Neither is a demonstrated Quran-internal bridge, so the honest result is unresolved at the root level with the substantive content stated per-class.
jwr.strongest_counterexample: 16:9:6:1 jaA}ir — «وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمِنْهَا جَآئِرٌ»: a way that swerves off-course, anchored to qaSd al-sabiyl (the straight/direct). It is semantically orthogonal to both populated senses (deviation is neither adjacency nor refuge) and is a single unreinforced occurrence, so it defeats any unified root nucleus. Secondary counterexample to a protection-centric unity: 13:4:4:1 mutajaAwiraAt — inanimate tracts of land merely adjoining, with no protective, social, or moral content, showing adjacency and refuge share no distributed entailment and the sole cross-class link is the one ambiguous nominal jaAr (protector 8:48 vs neighbor 4:36).
jwr.independent_verification: All 13 word_refs, forms (N=5, V(III)=1, V(IV)=6, V(X)=1), and verse_texts confirmed against the packet; the three lenses independently converged on no-single-nucleus and on 16:9 as the resistant isolate.

rkE.candidate_root_contribution: rkE denotes the visible, enacted bodily act/posture of bowing (bending/lowering the torso) performed as reverent submission before God, held categorically distinct from and lesser than full prostration (sjd), with which it is characteristically co-listed as a separate item. The finite verb names the act, the active participle raakiE- names its doer/state, and the fuEEal noun rukkaE names its performers collectively; all three shapes resolve to one nucleus.
rkE.plain_explanation: Across all 13 occurrences the root means 'to bow' as a devotional posture. The decisive Quran-internal signal is that bowing is repeatedly listed side-by-side with prostration (sjd) as a separate act (22:26, 2:125, 22:77, 3:43, 48:29, 9:112), so the two cannot be the same act and rkE is not prostration. It is also shown to be something seen and done ('you see them bowing', 48:29) and physically fallen into (38:24), not a purely inner attitude. The account is graded MODERATE rather than STRONG because the narrow 'posture-not-abstract-submission' claim cannot be adversarially cleaned (the root has no secular/neutral bending occurrence anywhere in the corpus), and 38:24 (fell down bowing and turned in repentance) materially pulls toward either attitude/contrition or prostration-type collapse.
rkE.strongest_counterexample: 38:24:31:1 'wa-kharra raakiEan wa-anaaba' (David fell down bowing and turned in repentance). This is the single materially resistant occurrence: it is the only individual, spontaneous, non-communal, non-liturgical token; the collocate kharra ('fell/collapsed down') connotes going all the way down, which fits the deeper posture (prostration) against which rkE is elsewhere the lesser bend, straining the rkE-not-sjd contrast; and the framing by anaaba (contrite turning) rather than salaat/sjd pulls raakiEan toward attitude ('in humbled abasement') rather than the defined ritual bend. Neither resolution -- loosening posture to attitude, or letting rkE cover collapse -- is Quran-internally excluded, so 38:24 caps the grade.
rkE.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each read all 13 occurrences; two of three (A, C) independently converged on MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE with 38:24 as the resistant seam, and all three agreed the competitor 'submission' account cannot be internally refuted.

$ml.plain_explanation: Within the Quran the root ش م ل appears as two morphologically and semantically distinct, internally coherent classes that share no Quran-internal bridge. (1) The nominal شِمَال/شَمَائِل (10/12) means 'the left' — a lateral side/hand/direction/group defined relationally as the counterpart of يَمِين (the right); in 7 of 10 tokens يمين/أيمان stands in the same verse (34:15, 18:17, 18:18, 50:17, 70:37, 16:48, 7:17), and the other 3 (56:41 ×2, 69:25) sit in a discourse built on the same right/left pair. (2) The Form VIII verb ٱشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَىٰ (2/12; 6:143, 6:144, one repeated formula) means 'to enclose/contain/comprise' — comprehensive interior containment (what the wombs enclose), with no directional or lateral content. The two classes not only fail to bridge but pull in opposite directions: the noun is partitive/contrastive (this side, not the other) while the verb is comprehensive/totalizing (all the contents within). No occurrence activates a shared 'covering/wrapping-to-a-side' nucleus; any nucleus broad enough to span both is a vague abstraction unsupported Quran-internally and reliant on barred external etymology. The honest result is UNRESOLVED at root level: two unbridged lexicalized classes, not one meaning.
$ml.strongest_counterexample: 6:143:15:1 / 6:144:13:1 «أَمَّا ٱشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَرْحَامُ ٱلْأُنثَيَيْنِ» is pure comprehensive containment with no lateral 'left' axis, while 34:15:10:2 «جَنَّتَانِ عَن يَمِينٍ وَشِمَالٍ» and 50:17:7:2 «عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ» are 'one of two opposed sides' with no containment — the two classes pull in opposite directions (partitive vs comprehensive) and neither reading transfers across the boundary, disproving any single unified nucleus.
$ml.independent_verification: Adversary Lens C independently attempted and failed to construct a Quran-internal unifying nucleus, corroborating Lenses A and B; all three agree on the unbridged two-class split.

Hnf.candidate_root_contribution: In the Quran the root ح-ن-ف surfaces only as the single lexicalized adjective ḥanīf (sg. حَنِيفًا) and its plural (حُنَفَاءَ), always a state-descriptor (ḥāl or kāna-predicate), never a verb, maṣdar, or other derivative. Its narrowest defensible sense is: the standing state of exclusive, non-associating devotion oriented to Allah alone — set against shirk and against confessional (Jewish/Christian) identity. This is a manner of orientation, distinct from and additional to submission (muslim), devotion (qānit), sincerity (mukhliṣ), and good-doing (muḥsin), all of which are named separately beside it.
Hnf.plain_explanation: Every one of the 12 occurrences is the same one adjective describing a person or community as exclusively turned to Allah alone, not associating anything with Him and not belonging to a named confession. It is a quality/posture, not an act, and it is always accompanied by an explicit exclusion of shirk or a statement of exclusive devotion. Because the whole root is a single frozen adjective locked in a near-identical formulaic environment, the account fits all uses cleanly but cannot be graded as an established root-wide semantics.
Hnf.strongest_counterexample: 3:67 (word_ref 3:67:9:1): 'mā kāna Ibrāhīmu yahūdiyyan wa-lā naṣrāniyyan wa-lākin kāna ḥanīfan musliman' — here ḥanīf sits inside a confessional taxonomy (yahūdī / naṣrānī / ḥanīf) and is paired with muslim (ḥanīfan musliman), pulling it toward a lexicalized Abrahamic identity label; the non-redundancy of the pairing still shows it contributes distinct anti-shirk exclusivity rather than 'submitter'. This is the occurrence that most resists a single compositional 'state-of-orientation' reading and most exposes how much the positive content is co-supplied by neighbouring terms.
Hnf.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (bottom-up A, distributional B, adversarial C) each returned no resistant sub-class and the same exclusivity nucleus; the plural cases (22:31, 98:5) independently corroborate the singular's meaning off the Abraham formula.

Sxr.candidate_root_contribution: A concrete, hard, solid, dense mass of stone — 'rock'. The root denotes a self-contained, immovable, impenetrable body/substance of stone, individuated by morphology as either the unit noun ṣakhrah (a single discrete rock-body/boulder: 18:63, 31:16) or the collective ṣakhr (rock as workable bedrock material: 89:9). All attested contexts (landmark, sealed interior, carved bedrock) reduce to this one substance without abstraction.
Sxr.plain_explanation: Every one of the three Quranic occurrences of ص خ ر is a noun meaning literally 'rock' — a hard, solid stone mass. It appears as a specific rock beside which travellers shelter (18:63), as the archetype of a sealed, impenetrable place where even a mustard-seed's weight could be hidden (31:16), and as the bedrock hewn by Thamud in the valley (89:9). The only variation is grammatical number/individuation: ṣakhrah names one rock-body, ṣakhr names rock as material. The core meaning 'hard solid rock' is stable across all three; nothing more abstract (e.g. 'hardness of heart') or any verbal/action sense is attested.
Sxr.strongest_counterexample: 89:9 (ٱلصَّخْرَ carved/hewn through by humans — rock as workable material) versus 31:16 (صَخْرَةٍ as the humanly-inaccessible ultimate hiding place — impenetrable sealed interior). Surface tension: workable vs. impenetrable. It fails to break the account because both frames presuppose the identical nucleus of hardness: in 31:16 the point is that only Allah retrieves what is sealed within hard rock, and in 89:9 the marvel/hubris is that Thamud managed to cut hard rock. The contrast reinforces rather than fractures the concrete 'hard rock' nucleus; no occurrence materially resists it.
Sxr.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) converged on the same concrete nucleus; A and C independently reached MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE on the lexicalized-nominal cap, corroborating the grade.

bhm.candidate_root_contribution: In the Quran the root bhm surfaces ONLY as the singular feminine noun bahiymah (qac_pos=N, no verb, no other derivation) and ONLY inside the frozen construct bahiymat al-anaam (bhm bound to the distinct root n-3-m). As a lexicalized-class term it denotes a category of grazing/pastoral livestock realized as lawful edible provision: provided as rizq (razaqahum, 22:28/22:34), eaten and given to the poor (fakuluu minhaa, 22:28), declared lawful (uhillat, 5:1), and offered with invocation of God's name (yadhkuruu isma llaah, 22:28/22:34). The ONLY internal contrast that fixes its field is bahiymat al-anaam (lawful) vs al-Sayd/game (restricted in ihram) in 5:1. Crucially, this is a lexicalized-class value, NOT a recovered productive root nucleus: because bahiymah never occurs free of al-anaam, never governs any other noun, and never predicates, the independent semantic contribution of bhm itself is underdetermined and not isolable Quran-internally.
bhm.plain_explanation: The root b-h-m appears only three times, always as the noun 'bahiymah' locked in one phrase 'bahiymat al-anaam' (the beast-stock of the grazing livestock). All three verses treat it as lawful, edible livestock given by God as provision and offered ritually; 5:1 adds the one contrast, distinguishing this permitted livestock from hunted game forbidden while in the sacred state. Because the word never stands alone, never varies in form (only its case ending changes for grammar), and is never a verb, we can describe the lexical item and its context confidently but cannot recover any independent meaning of the root itself. We deliberately reject the classical 'mute/inarticulate beast' sense: nothing in these verses touches speech, sound, or obscurity, and importing it would violate the Quran-internal source policy.
bhm.strongest_counterexample: There is no internal counterexample to a single-meaning reading: all three tokens are the same noun in the same construct, so consistency is trivial and evidentially cheap. The strongest adversarial fact is STRUCTURAL, targeting any isolable-nucleus or STRONG grade: 5:1:8:1 embeds bahiymat al-anaam in a bare legal-permission frame (uhillat lakum bahiymatu l-anaam) that strips away the razaqahum/ritual-slaughter scaffolding of 22:28 and 22:34, yet bahiymah contributes no new increment - the surrounding frame supplies all the force. This demonstrates that bahiymah behaves as a stable referential label fixed by collocation, and that the root's own contribution cannot be separated from al-anaam or falsified Quran-internally.
bhm.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, C) converged: all report one lexicalized nominal, one construct, one field, no isolable nucleus, and independently grade the positive claim at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE with the root nucleus UNRESOLVED.

fsH.candidate_root_contribution: fsH = to make/open accommodating space — create room in a shared locus by yielding/repositioning within it (not by leaving or rising from it). Domain-general as to WHAT is made roomy: realized as reflexive-distributive mutual room-making (Form V tafaʿʿul), plain transitive human act (Form I), and a divine reciprocal act of the same root with an unspecified space-domain.
fsH.plain_explanation: Every attested token of this root lives in one verse, 58:11 (al-Mujādila), in one scene: believers are told to make room in the sitting-assemblies (majālis), and God promises to make room for them in return. The narrowest reading that carries all three tokens is 'make/create accommodating space, open up room.' The Form V verb (تَفَسَّحُوا۟) and the Form I verb (فَٱفْسَحُوا۟) name and then execute the SAME act inside one sentence, which shows the form difference is valency/aspect (mutual-distributive vs plain), not two meanings. The divine token (يَفْسَحِ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ) mirrors the human act, so the root's reciprocal figure only works if it is one nucleus deployed across domains. The account is clean and morphologically triangulated within the scene, and it is sharply distinguished inside the verse from n-sh-z (rise/move up) and r-f-ʿ (raise in rank). It is capped at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE purely by breadth: the entire evidence base is a single verse and a single event, so no cross-context adversarial test is possible, and the divine token leaves a concrete-vs-abstract residue.
fsH.strongest_counterexample: At 58:11:11:1 (يَفْسَحِ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ) the agent is divine and the object is deleted, so the concrete seating-room reading of the human imperatives cannot be transferred literally; the token fits the nucleus only when it is pitched domain-general (make/create accommodating space), leaving concrete-vs-abstract expansiveness Quran-internally underdetermined.
fsH.independent_verification: All three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B nucleus, C adversarial) reached MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE, agreed the single verse forbids STRONG/UNIVERSAL, and agreed the divine token is the sole point of strain.

hzm.candidate_root_contribution: hzm (Form I) = the routing / breaking of a massed fighting body's cohesion so that it collapses and is put to flight. Active (hazamu, 2:251) = to rout / put a host to flight; passive and the maf`ul participle (yuhzamu 54:45, mahzum 38:11) = to be routed / put to flight. The patient is always a collective fighting force, and the manifest result is flight, not the host's destruction.
hzm.plain_explanation: Across all three occurrences hzm denotes one event: a massed military body is broken and routed. In 2:251 Talut's band 'routs them' (the enemy host) by God's leave; in 38:11 a 'host (jund) of the confederates' is described as 'routed (mahzum)'; in 54:45 'the assembly (al-jam`) will be routed and they will turn their backs.' The Quran supplies its own gloss of the event in 54:45 (turning the backs = flight) and, in 2:251, keeps hzm distinct from qatala (David's killing of Goliath), so hzm is the breaking-and-flight of the force, separable both from slaying and from the ensuing retreat. The only honest limitation is breadth: 3 tokens, all in a single battlefield domain.
hzm.strongest_counterexample: The strongest adversarial reading is hzm = 'destroy/annihilate' (folding in the killing of 2:251). It is refuted Quran-internally: 2:251 deploys qatala separately for David's slaying of Goliath (redundant if hzm already meant 'kill them'), and 54:45 immediately unpacks the routed host as fleeing survivors (wa-yuwalluna al-dubur), not the dead. A second candidate, that mahzum (38:11) is a frozen lexicalized epithet split from the verbal event, also fails: it is predicated directly of jund 'there' (hunalika, battlefield deixis) 'of the confederates', i.e. it is transparently the resultative of the same routing verb applied to the same participant type. No occurrence supports 'destroy', and no occurrence resists the single-nucleus reading.
hzm.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (bottom-up A, independent B, adversarial C) converged on the same unified nucleus and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade with no resistant occurrence; aggregator confirmed word_refs, forms, and verse_text against the packet.

jzA.candidate_root_contribution: In its sole attested realization — the singular indefinite noun juz' (جُزْء, hamzated), form N, 3/3 tokens — this packet denotes 'a part / portion: one partitive constituent of a larger specifiable whole.' The juz' is always a proper sub-portion (never the totality), framed by an explicit min-partitive naming the whole (min-hum 15:44, min-hunna 2:260, min 'ibādihi 43:15), and standing as the object or result of an act of dividing/assigning (maqsūm/q-s-m in 15:44; ij'al in 2:260; ja'alū in 43:15). It is valence-neutral and of no fixed magnitude. No verbal, plural, or other derivational form is attested, so no claim is made about a broader root-level (verbal/eventive) contribution.
jzA.plain_explanation: Every occurrence in this packet is the noun juz' meaning 'a part/portion of a whole' — a divided or assigned share of some larger set (people apportioned to Hell's gates, physical pieces of the four birds, a subset of God's servants falsely attributed to Him). Critically, despite the packet label 'ج ز ا / jzA', not one token carries the sense of recompense/reward/requital (jazā', a distinct root ج ز ي that is absent here); that gloss is an orthographic-label false prior to be excluded, not imported.
jzA.strongest_counterexample: 43:15:5:1 (min 'ibādihi juz'an). Unlike the enumerated apportionment of 15:44 and the concrete physical fragment of 2:260, nothing is literally divided here; juz' names an attributed/derivative constituent of God (offspring), which could be read as a mere subset ('some of His servants') with no real partition — threatening the partition/division component of the nucleus. It bends but does not break the account: the polemic ('inna l-insāna la-kafūrun mubīn') is intelligible only if juz' means 'a constituent part making up a whole,' and the surface min 'ibādihi preserves the partitive-of-a-whole frame. It therefore defeats the narrower 'physical severed piece' reading and caps the nucleus at the more abstract 'constituent portion of a specifiable whole,' rather than establishing a resistant second class.
jzA.independent_verification: Three independent lenses (Analyst A bottom-up, Analyst B, Adversary C) converged on the identical nucleus, the identical exclusion of the recompense prior, and the identical MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE ceiling; the adversary's explicit disprove attempt could not break the unity.
